Score of the single-cell log-likelihood in \(\boldsymbol{p}\)

Source: R/02_02_single_cell_decovart_estimate_ratios.R
gradient_loglik_single_cell.Rd

With \(\boldsymbol{W}=\boldsymbol{S}_W(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1}\) and \(\boldsymbol{r}=\boldsymbol{y}-c\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}\boldsymbol{p}\), $$ U_j = \phi^{-1}\bigl( c\,\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}^{\top}\boldsymbol{W}\boldsymbol{r} +\tfrac{1}{2} \boldsymbol{r}^{\top}\boldsymbol{W}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j \boldsymbol{W}\boldsymbol{r} \bigr) -\tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{tr}(\boldsymbol{W}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j). $$ This is the score in the article. It is not gradient_loglik_unconstrained(), whose trace term carries an extra \(p_j\) because \(\partial\boldsymbol{\Sigma}/\partial p_j =2p_j\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\).

Usage

gradient_loglik_single_cell(
  p,
  y,
  mean_signature_matrix,
  Sigma,
  mean_scale,
  variance_scale
)

Arguments

p

Composition of length \(J\). It does not have to sum to 1 (numerical derivatives step off the simplex).

y

Bulk vector of length \(G\).

mean_signature_matrix

Reference mean, \(G\times J\).

Sigma

Cell-level covariances, \(G\times G\times J\).

mean_scale

Positive plug-in \(c=an\).

variance_scale

Positive plug-in \(\phi=a^2 n\).

Value

Numeric vector of length \(J\).
